_comment_: Citation source-of-truth. Per-paper entries used in disclaimers and source panels.
_comment_deep_reading_: The seven entries below were added for the `reading` network and the `deepreading` overlay, and all were read in full first. Two naming traps to avoid: (1) `simony-2016` is the Nature Communications paper on DMN reconfiguration during narrative; the pre-existing `hasson-2016` is a different paper, a Trends in Cognitive Sciences review, and Uri Hasson is senior author on both. Do not merge them. (2) `wolf-2018` is a trade book, so it is tagged SECONDARY-ONLY on purpose — it synthesises other people's imaging rather than reporting any, and citing it drags the overlay's computed tier to `partial`. That is the correct outcome and should not be papered over by retagging.

wolf-2018.title: Reader, Come Home: The Reading Brain in a Digital World
wolf-2018.note: Letters Two and Three read in full. Source of the term 'deep reading' as used here and of its three-family taxonomy: evocative (imagery, empathy and perspective-taking, background knowledge), analytical (analogy and inference, critical analysis) and generative (insight). Wolf states outright that these 'are not meant as an exclusive list, nor do they appear in the brain in any single sequence or configuration' — the sentence this overlay is built on. A trade book reporting no imaging of its own: its neural claims are glosses of other people's work, several at popular-science remove (mirror neurons; a Psychological Bulletin review whose conclusion she quotes as 'creativity is everywhere'). Treat as the source for the construct, never for the anatomy. It also misattributes the Konrath empathy meta-analysis to Stanford.

dehaene-2014.title: Reading in the Brain Revised and Extended: Response to Comments
dehaene-2014.note: Source for the cortical-competition claim: as literacy rises, responses to faces fall in the left hemisphere and rise in the right FFA, so words and faces compete for territory in the left occipitotemporal sulcus. Dehaene goes further and suggests part or all of the right-lateralisation of face recognition is itself a consequence of literacy, since most fMRI studies scan highly literate graduate students. Also the source for the VWFA's connectivity constraint (its fibres preferentially target left superior temporal and inferior frontal language areas) and for a left premotor contribution to reading handwritten script.

reich-2011.title: A ventral visual stream reading center independent of visual experience
reich-2011.note: Eight congenitally blind subjects reading Braille peaked in the VWFA, within 1-2 functional voxels of the canonical sighted location, and stayed left-lateralised whichever hand they read with. Braille words beat a verb-generation control in the same region, so the response is reading-specific rather than general language. The authors propose 'metamodal word form area' as the better name. Reports Talairach, not MNI: sighted (-42, -57, -6), blind (-38, -60, -8).

dehaene-lambertz-2018.title: The emergence of the visual word form: Longitudinal evolution of category-specific ventral visual areas during reading acquisition
dehaene-lambertz-2018.note: Ten children scanned across seven sessions through their first year of reading. Word-evoked activation rose across sessions in left fusiform (MNI -42 -50 -22) among other sites, and 8 of 10 showed a VWFA cluster once reading was established. Independently reproduces the face-displacement result longitudinally: as reading speed rose, responses to faces increased in the *right* fusiform. Reports MNI; the parcel stores Reich's Talairach instead, since one parcel may not hold both spaces.

tamir-2016.title: Reading fiction and reading minds: the role of simulation in the default network
tamir-2016.note: Splits literary reading across two default-network subsystems: the medial temporal lobe subsystem tracked how vividly a passage described a scene, the dorsomedial prefrontal subsystem tracked whether it described people and minds. The core subsystem tracked neither. Two things the headline glosses: the dmPFC subsystem responded more strongly to abstract than to vivid passages, and that effect (d=1.07) was about twice the size of the social effect (d=0.57). The authors' own limitations: n=26, so the brain-behaviour and mediation estimates 'may be overestimates of the true population effect', the design is cross-sectional and cannot establish causal direction, and a reverse model in which theory of mind drives fiction reading remains viable.

simony-2016.authors: Simony, Honey, Chen, Lositsky, Yeshurun, Wiesel & Hasson
simony-2016.title: Dynamic reconfiguration of the default mode network during narrative comprehension
simony-2016.note: Default-network coupling tracked narrative coherence: absent at rest and under word-scrambling, present under paragraph-scrambling and the intact story. Coupling was history-dependent in the default network but not in auditory cortex, and its strength per story segment predicted later recall of that segment (r=0.6, q(FWER)<0.02). Scope limit that matters for a reading figure: the stimulus was a spoken story, not text. n=18 for the imaging, a separate n=30 for the memory test.

yao-2011.title: Silent reading of direct versus indirect speech activates voice-selective areas in the auditory cortex
yao-2011.note: The inner voice, measured. Silent reading of direct speech ('Mary said: I am hungry') drove voice-selective right auditory cortex harder than meaning-equivalent indirect speech, in two clusters along posterior and middle right STS, with the regions defined per subject by a Belin 2000 voice localiser. Not a difficulty effect: reading time per word and comprehension accuracy did not differ. Clearly right-lateralised, which the authors contrast with earlier imagery studies that found bilateral or left-dominant patterns and attribute to their task requiring no metacognitive judgement. 16 of 26 subjects survived exclusion.

parsons-2001.title: New evidence for distinct right and left brain systems for deductive versus probabilistic reasoning

saxe-2003.title: People thinking about thinking people: the role of the temporo-parietal junction in 'theory of mind'
saxe-2003.note: Establishes bilateral TPJ robustly and says the left and right did not differ on the belief contrast; its only laterality finding is that left TPJ responded selectively to verbal descriptions while right also picked up photographs. It does NOT establish the wider ToM network — its MPFC and precuneus results are single midline coordinates, one tied to person-detection rather than mentalising, and the precuneus effect was a deactivation the authors called ambiguous and dropped. Cite it for TPJ; the region set comes from Dufour 2013.

_comment_access_tags_: Entries below carry an `access` field per the Source Transparency Protocol (vault CLAUDE.md). PRIMARY-FULL = the PDF was read end to end in the session that added the citation. SECONDARY-ONLY = the citation was harvested from a reference list in a paper that WAS read, and the source itself has not been opened. The cortical-networks view surfaces this distinction per network so the figure never implies more grounding than it has. Entries above this comment predate the convention and are untagged.

kean-2026.title: Evidence from formal logical reasoning reveals that the language of thought is not natural language

fedorenko-2024.title: Language is primarily a tool for communication rather than thought

paunov-2019.title: Functionally distinct language and Theory of Mind networks are synchronized at rest and during language comprehension

mineroff-2018.title: A robust dissociation among the language, multiple demand, and default mode networks

dufour-2013.title: Similar brain activation during false belief tasks in a large sample of adults with and without autism
dufour-2013.note: Read in full; every ROI and coordinate previously extracted from PubMed Central confirmed exactly. Defines seven ToM ROIs including a middle MPFC band and a right anterior STS, both of which the figure was missing until 2026-08-05. Treats DMPFC and precuneus as single midline ROIs rather than left/right pairs. Individual-subject identification rates vary widely: RTPJ 94%, PC 91%, LTPJ 87%, RSTS 85%, DMPFC 68%, MMPFC 64%, VMPFC 55%.

deen-2015.title: Functional organization of social perception and cognition in the superior temporal sulcus

pritchett-2018.title: High-level language processing regions are not engaged in action observation or imitation
pritchett-2018.note: Read in full. The angular gyrus exception is narrower than the abstract suggests: it holds in one experiment of four (passive viewing of naturalistic face and body videos) and does NOT appear for imitation anywhere. In that same experiment every language region showed small but reliable above-baseline responses, so 'little or no response' means not exceeding the nonword control and falling far below sentences, rather than silence. The paper also treats the angular gyrus's membership of the language network as contested, and keeps speech-articulation cortex, speech-perception cortex and the high-level language network as three separate systems — do not collapse them.

jouravlev-2019.title: Speech-accompanying gestures are not processed by the language-processing mechanisms
jouravlev-2019.note: Every stimulus had the speaker's face masked with a beige rectangle, so this paper contains no data on face, gaze or expression perception and must not be cited for them. Its Discussion argues that faces, body postures, voices, prosody and gesture are handled by functionally distinct regions, which is why the `face` network was renamed and its copy reworked.

shain-2023.title: No evidence of theory of mind reasoning in the human language network

buckner-2019.title: The brain's default network: updated anatomy, physiology and evolving insights

zatorre-belin-chapter.title: Auditory cortex processing streams: where are they and what do they do?
zatorre-belin-chapter.venue: In: Plasticity and Signal Representation in the Auditory System (Springer US), pp. 277-290
zatorre-belin-chapter.note: Container identified 2026-08-05 and confirmed against Crossref: the page range 277-290 matches the PDF exactly. ISBN 9780387231549. Crossref carries no publication year for this chapter; internal citations to J Neurosci vol 24 put it at 2004 or later. Supply the year before using this in print.

chen-2023.authors: Chen, Affourtit, Ryskin, Regev, Norman-Haignere, Jouravlev, Malik-Moraleda, Kean, Varley & Fedorenko
chen-2023.title: The human language system, including its inferior frontal component in "Broca's area," does not support music perception
chen-2023.note: Read in full. Note three small non-null results the headline conclusion glosses: scrambled melodies drew a slightly LARGER network response than intact ones (p=0.046, reversed direction), sour-note vs well-formed reached significance at network level (p=0.037) though not per-region, and Mandarin speakers showed above-baseline music responses in two language fROIs. The music-vs-animal-sounds comparison is p=0.056, a trend rather than a difference — an earlier version of the figure's copy overstated this. Authors also restrict the claim to the high-level language network, explicitly excluding speech perception and prosody.

norman-haignere-2015.title: Distinct cortical pathways for music and speech revealed by hypothesis-free voxel decomposition
norman-haignere-2015.note: Read in full; the planum polare / left planum temporale placement and the p=0.055 laterality trend were confirmed verbatim. Three scope limits worth keeping in view: the paper reports NO coordinates of any kind, only relative anatomy against primary auditory cortex; its maps are smoothed group-averaged continuous weights rather than discrete parcels, so three spheres imply more anatomical consistency than it claims; and its lateral component is SPEECH-selective (phonemes and syllables), not prosody — the word prosody never appears. Subjects were non-musicians by design.

rugg-2013.title: Brain networks underlying episodic memory retrieval

andrews-hanna-2014.title: The default network and self-generated thought: component processes, dynamic control, and clinical relevance
andrews-hanna-2014.venue: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences

parvizi-2026.title: Functional architecture of the human insula revealed by causal intracranial mapping
parvizi-2026.caution: Unreviewed preprint. Splits the anterior insula into two functionally distinct zones and prefers 'action mode network' to 'salience network'. Cited here as a caveat against treating the anterior insula as one node, not as support for the salience grouping.

_comment_verified_2026_08_05_: The five entries below were originally added from model background knowledge with recalled citations. On 2026-08-05 every one was checked against the publisher or PubMed record: authors, title, venue, volume, pages and DOI all matched. Belin, Sammler, Kanwisher, Craig and Seeley are PRIMARY-PARTIAL — citation confirmed and abstract read, full text paywalled. Phelps & LeDoux was then supplied as a PDF and read in full. Verifying a citation is not the same as verifying the claim hung on it: the emotion network these partly supported was dropped because no source tested its grouping.
